extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: An open-source reasoning dataset for training models on math, code, and science questions. It was created by systematically exploring data curation choices such as question sourcing, filtering, deduplication, answer sampling, and teacher model selection.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper describes a data generation pipeline that sources questions from multiple existing datasets and web forums, including synthetic, semi-synthetic, and human-written sources. It also generates reasoning traces with annotator models and explores finding reasoning traces from the web by searching DCLM-RefinedWeb/CommonCrawl-derived text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For sources that produce fewer datapoints, the questions were repeated until the desired amount was reached.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions and text from existing sources across code, math, and science domains, including StackExchange, OpenCodeReasoning, NuminaMath, MathPile, Organic Chemistry PDFs/textbooks, CommonCrawl-derived DCLM-RefinedWeb, and other curated or synthetic datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper describes generating multiple answers for each question using teacher models, then in some experiments re-annotating or verifying samples with Claude 3.7 or GPT-4o-mini. For code, it says they "re-annotated 10K random coding problems" with Claude and verified them; for filtering/verification, they ask GPT-4o-mini to judge correctness, English-only, long paragraphs, or majority consensus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The section reports verification and ablation analyses of annotation choices, including comparisons of Claude vs R1 as annotator, GPT-4o-mini verification, and teacher-model ablations; however, no inter-annotator agreement metric is reported.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For some code experiments, 16 candidate solutions per question were considered; for the Claude re-annotation experiment, 10K coding problems were re-annotated and verified. The section does not state a standard number of human labels per item.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Claude 3.7 (with thinking mode), DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, GPT-4o-mini, and FastText were used in annotation/filtering/verification workflows.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The pipeline may assume cross-domain transfer when selecting strategies that maximize overall average benchmark performance rather than domain-specific performance; the authors note it is unclear whether this transfer persists once domains are mixed.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The work did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning or staged SFT/curriculum learning. The authors also note open questions about cross-domain transfer, scaling behavior near teacher performance, and how question diversity interacts with answer diversity across domains, dataset sizes, and model scales.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as supporting safer open-source reasoning models by evaluating whether models refuse unsafe requests while complying with benign requests.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) reasoning models in science, math, and code domains; the paper also discusses filtering and verification strategies for training downstream models and evaluating them on benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Deduplication and repeated teacher sampling were used; the pipeline explores no deduplication, exact match deduplication, and fuzzy deduplication, with multiple answers per question at 1×, 4×, and 16×. The final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains, exact deduplication for math and science, and no deduplication for code.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to select high-quality subsets using methods such as difficulty-based filtering and response-length filtering; for code, difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini was used, and for math and science, response-length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini was used. The pipeline also performs decontamination by discarding samples marked contaminated by either normalized Indel similarity or 13-gram overlap.
